messages:
maya: FYI I noticed a weird regression on the golden set after landing the quantized-kernel change earlier. variance/entropy up ~12% on a handful of inputs.
ravi: can you paste an example input + outputs? is this across all golden shards or just one?
maya: one failing shard so far. sample input: \"Summarize the policy on data retention for enterprise customers.\" output before:\n\"We retain logs for 90 days...\" output after:\n\"We continue to store logs... [more verbose/changed framing]\"
maya: not a catastrophic drift, but enough to flip some eval thresholds and trigger alerts :grimacing:
bench-bot: (automated) perf-check: quant-kernel v3.4 deployed at 1729001200; avg latency +0.8ms; token cost -6%. No smoke failures flagged by golden-compare for 95% shard coverage.
sam: interesting that perf improved but quality drifted. could be tokenizer changes or binding order in kernels.
ingrid: did any of the onboarding transforms change? e.g., padding/truncation or special-token handling?
maya: no changes in tokenizer on our side. the kernel change reordered attention kernel selection for seqlen>512 fallback.
devon: maybe KV-cache ordering subtlely changes attention weights for edge prompts. we should run a targeted diff across the failure shard.
ravi: agree. maya can you run the reproduce command with current runtime flags and include --record-activations? example:
```
./bench/run_golden_compare --shard 42 --model rwd-bert-q --flags "--kernel-policy=latest --record-activations"
```
maya: running now, will post artifacts. ETA ~10m.
bench-bot: (automated) queued job 987654321 for shard 42. link: https://ci.redwood/runs/987654321
maya: results: activation diffs show minor float reorderings in attention weights at layer 9, positions 124-130. KL divergence per-token spikes correlated with the entropy bump.
ingrid: that points to numerical nondeterminism after kernel reorder. we need to decide: roll back kernel order, add deterministic fallback for golden runs, or expand tolerance in evals.
sam: expanding eval tolerance is slippery — masks real regressions. prefer either deterministic golden hook or revert.
devon: could we add a deterministic compare mode where we force legacy kernel selection for golden shards only? config by env var on bench runner.
ravi: implement plan: 1) maya/ingrid add a bench-only flag `FORCE_LEGACY_KERNEL=1` to reproduce and run full golden sweep. 2) sam/devon prepare a small patch to make kernel selection stable across builds (deterministic tie-break). 3) if patch is low-risk, can ship; else revert ordering.
maya: created draft PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4321 with the FORCE_LEGACY_KERNEL flag and repro logs attached.
bench-bot: (automated) golden-sweep queued (full coverage) with legacy hook, run id 987654322.
maya: full sweep with legacy hook shows no regression on other shards. current quant-kernel ordering is the likely cause.
sam: thanks. devon/sam will prioritize deterministic tie-break. if that lands quickly, we can keep quant improvements.
devon: working on deterministic tie-break now; small change to kernel_priority comparator and added unit test. will request review from @sam @ingrid.
ingrid: also let's add a note in onboarding docs re: "avoid non-deterministic kernel selection in canonical evals" — I'll update onboarding checklist.
ravi: one operational thing: we should add a post-onboard smoke that runs golden-shard compare with FORCE_LEGACY_KERNEL and without, and diffs must be small (<1% tokens change) before admission.
maya: agreed, I'll file an intake checklist ticket.
onboard-bot: (system) ticket #INT-834 filed: "golden smoke: dual-kernel comparison required for quantized kernel changes" assigned to eng-ml.
maya: tl;dr: regression tracked to kernel-order nondeterminism; short-term: reproduce + block; medium: deterministic comparator change; long-term: add dual-kernel smoke gate in onboarding pipeline. thanks all :thumbsup:
